role_in_parent: Provides the well-defined inverse map needed in every later case lemma and in the final theorem statement.
statement_nl: Let p be a prime and let k be an integer with 1 <= k <= p-1. Then there exists a unique integer I(k) in {1,2,...,p-1} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p).

domain_restrictions: p is a prime integer (so p >= 2)
k is an integer with 1 <= k <= p-1 (so k represents a nonzero residue class mod p)
I(k) is required to be an integer in the set {1,2,...,p-1} (a canonical representative of a residue class)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every prime p and every integer k with 1 <= k <= p-1 there exists a unique integer I in {1,...,p-1} (depending on p and k) such that k * I ≡ 1 (mod p).
quantifier_order: forall k (k is an integer with 1 <= k <= p-1)
there exists a unique I (integer with 1 <= I <= p-1) such that k * I ≡ 1 (mod p)

variables.name: k
variables.role: input element (representative of a nonzero residue class mod p)

variables.name: I(k)
variables.role: existential witness (multiplicative inverse of k modulo p), depends on p and k

witness_dependencies: I(k) depends on both p and k (written I = I_p(k) if one wants to emphasize dependence on modulus)
the witness I is unique within the specific set {1,...,p-1}; equivalently unique modulo p up to the chosen representative
existence of I is equivalent to gcd(k,p)=1, which holds because p is prime and 1 <= k <= p-1
